text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Farms in the Mekong Delta have harvested a bumper winter-spring crop with seven million tonnes of rice, an increase of more than 500,000 tonnes over last year's crop.

-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has told government officials to be thorough and fair in implementing new tax concessions aimed at attracting more foreign technology, expertise and investment to the setting up and operation of industrial zones, high-tech zones and export-processing zones.
-- Vietnam will be the third largest recipient of Australian aid in 1997-1998 with $46.2 million aid provided.
-- Japan's External Trade Organization says it wishes to help Vietnam develop into an electronic components manufacturing and exporting country.
-- Vietnam's Ambassador to the United States Le Van Bang presented his credentials to President Bill Clinton on Wednesday.
-- Officials have selected three songs all named "ASEAN song" from 80 songs about this topic, for a competition for the best official song for ASEAN.
-- Vietnam will launch a No-Tobacco week later this month to mark a worldwide No-Smoking day.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's acting mayor, Vo Viet Thanh, received Swedish Environment Minister Anna Lindh and members of her delegation on Thursday.
